column1: # What our code CALLS, and how the image is meant to provide it.
# Three defects in one day - `user-dirs.dirs` never written, `(unset)` swallowing
# the keyboard layout, polkitd simply absent so the power menu could not authorise
# a suspend - and each was found by a different accident, none by a check. The
# common cause is that our runtime dependencies are implicit: we know what we
# Cargo.toml, and we had never written down what the shipped system must PROVIDE
# for our own code to run.
# So this is that list. Enumerating it on 12 Aug found TWENTY-ONE of thirty-three
# external binaries absent from the image, including every one behind networking,
# audio, the clipboard and opening a file. None of those failures is loud: a
# missing binary is `No such file or directory` at spawn, inside a feature nobody
#   what      the binary name our code passes to Command::new
#   package   the Debian package that must be named in mkosi.conf `Packages=`
#             (`-` when the entry is `absent`, or when we ship the binary ourselves)
#   who       the component that calls it
#   status    ships   -> must be on the image; check fails if the package is unnamed
#             own     -> we build and stage it ourselves, not a distro package
#             base    -> guaranteed by the base system (coreutils, dpkg, systemd)
#             absent  -> deliberately not on this image; the reason is the last column
#   why       for `absent`, what breaks and why that is acceptable for now
# An `absent` line is a DECISION, not a shrug: it says the feature does not work on
# this image and somebody chose that. Turning one into `ships` is how a feature
